result.summary: The street features narrow sidewalks on both sides, with significant obstruction from parked vehicles on the right side encroaching on the walkway. While the narrow roadway likely keeps vehicle speeds low, the lack of marked crosswalks and poor sightlines at the intersection create risks for pedestrians.

hazards.name: Sidewalk Obstruction
hazards.description: Vehicles parked nose-in on the right side appear to overhang the sidewalk, significantly narrowing the usable walking space.

hazards.description: The intersection ahead lacks painted crosswalks, which reduces driver awareness of pedestrian crossing points.

interventions.title: High-Visibility Crosswalks
interventions.description: Install zebra-striped crosswalks at all legs of the intersection to clearly define pedestrian space.

interventions.title: Curb Extensions (Bulb-outs)
interventions.description: Install curb extensions at the corners to shorten crossing distances and improve sightlines by preventing parking at the intersection.

interventions.title: Parking Enforcement/Barriers
interventions.description: Install bollards or wheel stops to prevent vehicles from overhanging and obstructing the sidewalk on the right side.

result.summary: The pedestrian environment is characterized by an extremely narrow sidewalk that is further constrained by utility poles and parked vehicles. The lack of a buffer between the walkway and the roadway, combined with the absence of greenery, creates a functional but uncomfortable and inaccessible space for pedestrians.

hazards.name: Utility Pole Obstruction
hazards.description: A large wooden utility pole is situated directly in the center of the narrow sidewalk, blocking the path for pedestrians, especially those with mobility aids or strollers.

hazards.name: Substandard Sidewalk Width
hazards.description: The sidewalk is extremely narrow, providing insufficient space for pedestrians to pass one another comfortably or safely.

hazards.name: Lack of Pedestrian Buffer
hazards.description: There is no physical separation or buffer zone between the narrow walkway and the parked/moving vehicles.
hazards.location_in_image: Edge of the sidewalk adjacent to parked cars

interventions.description: Expand the sidewalk width to meet ADA standards, providing a clear and accessible path of travel.
